headline: Banks defying 4% interest spread cap, average gap nears 6%
summary: Bangladeshi banks are defying a 4% interest spread cap, with the average gap nearing 6%. Foreign banks recorded the highest average spread at 8.19%, followed by state-owned banks at 5.70% and private banks at 5.56%.
why: The interest rate spread, the gap between lending and deposit rates, is a key measure of bank profitability and borrowing costs. Regulatory caps on spreads affect lending margins for Bangladeshi banks.
